items.title: CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
items.snippet:
CISA has added two new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

items.title: Critical Linux kernel flaw allows remote root attacks on MPTCP servers
items.snippet: Security researchers at Anthropic have developed an exploit for a critical Linux kernel vulnerability that allows unauthenticated attackers to remotely execute commands as root on servers running Multipath TCP (MPTCP) listeners. [...]
items.summary: Anthropic researchers developed an exploit for a critical Linux kernel vulnerability that may let unauthenticated attackers remotely run commands as root on MPTCP listener servers.
items.why: Check whether servers run MPTCP listeners and prioritize investigating exposure to this kernel vulnerability.

items.title: Malicious Claude Code extension on Cursor planted SSH backdoors
items.snippet: A malicious version of Anthropic's Claude Code VS Code extension was distributed through Cursor's extension marketplace for approximately 11 hours on October 29, exposing up to 5,000 developers to malware designed to install persistent SSH backdoors. [...]

items.why: Check installed extensions and investigate unexpected SSH access or persistence.

learn.explainer: Multipath TCP (MPTCP) is the networking protocol named in the Linux vulnerability report. The snippet identifies servers running MPTCP listeners as potentially affected.
A UCAV is an unmanned combat aerial vehicle. The snippet describes North Korea displaying reconnaissance and attack drones, including a stealthy UCAV concept.
Patriot interceptors are missiles described in the item as American-made weapons for downing ballistic missiles. The report concerns US approval of their sale to Ukraine.

analysis.headline: Security, military capability and geopolitical signals
paragraphs: The stories span technical exposure, military systems and political tensions. The Linux kernel report describes a route to remote root access on MPTCP listeners, while the CISA item signals vulnerabilities added to its exploited-vulnerability catalog. Together, they underscore the value of checking exposure and acting on vulnerability guidance.

Military reporting presents distinct operational signals: China claims a GJ-21 drone launch and recovery from a Type 076 ship, while the US approved a Patriot missile sale to Ukraine. These reports concern different capabilities; the snippets do not establish a direct connection between them.

The G20 dispute and reporting on a suspected crypto theft linked to North Korea add political and cyber dimensions. For analysts, attribution and claims should remain qualified. Watch for further details on the vulnerability, the drone claim, and the terms and implementation of the missile sale.
takeaways: Check MPTCP exposure and review vulnerability guidance.
Treat operational claims as claims until supported by further details.
Track the distinct military and diplomatic developments without assuming a connection.
